correctness.rationale: From the grounded block matrix the two class-constant eigenvalues (when both blocks remain) have sum p+q+a and product 2p+a(q−2+a); contrast eigenvalues are p and p+q. Handling the empty blocks separately gives the same stated orbit spectra in their proper form. The mixed-minus-clique reciprocal prefix gaps are positive for k≤q−1 and have sign p−2 thereafter. Independent-minus-clique gaps for q≥3 are positive through k=q−1 and thereafter equal (q−4)/(2p)+1/(p+q); the sole negative full-sum case is (2,3), and equality only at (3,3). At q=2 independent leaders dominate both alternatives in weak submajorization with strict full-sum comparisons. Strict power comparison for r>1 follows from integrating the upper-tail sums (x−t)_+, which have nonnegative differences and are strictly ordered on an interval for the distinct reciprocal vectors. For (2,3) the mixed orbit never wins, and the difference between independent and clique orbits has sign given by the strictly convex function f(r)=2^r+2^(−r)+(2/5)^r−3, with f(0)=0, f(1)<0<f(2). This proves the unique crossing and the listed ties. The quoted approximate decimal is off by about 1.2×10^(−16); the exact defining equation and all classifications are unaffected.
residual_risks: Numerical checks are bounded; the all-size and continuous-order claims rely on the exact prefix and convexity arguments.
